The questions buyers ask

What would you
like to understand?

A clear boundary is part of a useful review.

All questions
Is SKUDocket an operating product?

SKUDocket is a research-stage concept. This website demonstrates a proposed workflow with fictional records. Demand, accepted pricing, live integrations, and production compliance coverage have not been demonstrated.

Who is this for?

US importer-of-record compliance leads handling recurring goods, multiple suppliers, and a customs broker. The starting test is one permissioned repeat-SKU US import lane.

Does it replace our customs broker?

The proposed dossier is prepared for broker review. The importer retains reasonable-care responsibility, and broker or counsel judgment remains part of the workflow.

Are the classifications binding?

No. Suggested rationales are nonbinding. The preview leaves code candidates unassigned; actual classification requires detailed facts and appropriate professional review.

What does a screening no-match mean?

It describes the specified search, sources, and date only. The CSL is an aid, not final clearance. Apparent matches need additional diligence and official-list checks.

What if origin evidence is missing?

The record stays held, with a named owner and next action. Available evidence, reviewed evidence, and preference eligibility are separate states.

How are source dates shown?

Version or edition, publication date, effective date, and retrieval date are distinct fields. Tariff and screening examples use explicitly simulated fixtures dated 01 Oct 2026.

What does the packet include?

A source manifest, product facts, invoice and valuation assumptions, competing classification rationales, origin and screening evidence, reviewer history, and open questions.

Can the demo file, send, or write to another system?

No. Local preview and synthetic PDF download are the only outputs. Filing, real messages, payments, and ERP or bank writes are unavailable.

Are integrations available?

No production integration is claimed. A future pilot would need a permissioned SKU feed; CSV, ERP, and e-commerce input routes remain scoping questions.

Is the pricing an active offer?

No. $3,000 for ten SKUs and $750–$2,500 per repeat lane per month are hypothetical test prices. There is no checkout or automatic renewal.

What makes a pilot proceed?

Legal and data licensing must permit the selected lane, the broker must incorporate dossiers, the importer must fund a scoped pilot, and a usable permissioned feed must be available.

How do I delete inquiry data?

These preview forms do not send or store inquiry data. Close the preview or clear the fields. The demo reset clears its local synthetic state. A live inquiry service will require an identified operator and working deletion route before collection.
